contents.text:
I'm checking the format rules: prose for explanations, with lists only for steps and choices. I'm also trying to pin down which section of /how-it-works covers packs, since I'm not certain of the exact address.

I'm weighing whether to guess the exact address of the packs section or use a lookup, and deciding I'll keep it simple: answer, cite the doc, and close with two or three choices, since every answer has to end that way.

ADR 0027 splits the framework into three parts. The engine holds the loop, sessions, usage, guards and contracts. It names no product and no country. An identity says who an agent is. A pack says what an agent can do.

The decision was made because Puls had grown inside the engine. Ten of its prompts, the shop tools and a South African time zone default lived in `LouisAgent.Core`. Every product built on the engine would have carried Puls with it.

Under the decision:

- An identity (`IAgentIdentity`) holds its voice, modes, roles and the packs it uses, by name.
- A pack (`IAgentPack`) holds toolsets, providers, guides and settings. It never references another pack or an identity.
- A host picks identities and packs at start-up with `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS`. One composition project, `src/hosts/LouisAgent.Composition`, knows them all.

The consequences: a product is configured, not coded. A new identity or pack adds no branch to the core. Identities and packs load only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change mid-conversation.

Source: `src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md`
